查看原文（19行） ```text **Three hard guarantees** - 🛡️ **Contract pre-check → rollback point → auto-rollback.** A data-driven **contract pre-check** runs first (message contract / dependency API / config schema / removed API / loader contract); then config backup + a full-tree **rollback point**. A failed install or relaunch **auto-rolls the tree back**, a 「roll back to previous」 button restores the last version, and plugins the new framework cannot load are **auto-disabled** — version check catches fake success, 15-min timeout + stall detection. - 👁️ **Even when another update channel changes the framework.** An **environment fingerprint** catches changes made by the official desktop updater or a manual `pnpm`: it auto-runs a **read-only pre-flight**, and disables a row **only with hard evidence** (package unresolvable / `file://` target gone / named in a boot-failure log). `@deepseek-ai/*` and **protected / core rows are never auto-disabled**; each auto-disable writes a one-command recovery record. - 🔒 **Plugin install & upgrade gating.** Version/declaration gate (`dsh.engines.framework` / `engines.dsh` / `@deepseek-ai/*` ranges, built-in zero-dependency semver), a **repo-size gate** on source channels, and explicit handling of **non-registry sources** — a bare version is written back only once the registry really resolves it, otherwise the package is materialized as `link:`. Install scripts are never auto-authorized, and pnpm's supply-chain gate is never bypassed. ```

If you just want to *use* a plugin, an ordinary install is simpler. - **What it pins**: the local artifact is written into the profile manifest `dependencies` (`link:`) and gets a matching entry in `pnpm-lock.yaml` — so lockfile health checks and rebuilds never treat it as an orphan, and it **survives restarts and instance updates**. - **What the console completes for it** (otherwise the usual outcome is "installed, but it will not load"): - **the target directory's own `dependencies`**: one install run inside that directory, filling in what the local directory is missing; - **the framework peer shim root**: when the local directory lives **outside** the profile tree, Node's resolution chain never reaches the profile's `node_modules`. The console links the framework peers it **declares and currently cannot resolve** (`@deepseek-ai/*`) at the **plugin root**, pointing at `~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/`. It is a **link**, not a copy — both sides share the same realpath, so Cordis service classes and LLM error classes keep their **module identity shared with the host**. - **Boundaries** (always reported honestly, never faked): - moving or deleting the local directory **breaks** the link (the manifest `link:` then points at a path that no longer exists); - shims only fill peers it **declares** and that are genuinely missing; a package the framework side does not have is never invented; - anything **already present** at the target path (including a dangling link) is **never overwritten** — it is skipped and reported; - **uninstall removes the shims the console created** (only its own; links you placed by hand are never touched); - if completion fails (target directory not writable, dependency install failed, …) the **install still completes**, and the result honestly says "not ready + what is missing" together with an action you can run. ### Static index market (plugin & skill tabs) > **Hybrid architecture**: browsing uses the static index (instant, zero GitHub API calls), > searching uses live channels (GitHub search API / multi-source parallel) — they complement > each other: a brand-new repo can be found by live search even before it enters the index. - Empty query on the GitHub source shows the **static index** (`marketplace/index.json`, jsDelivr CDN + 10-min host cache): 500+ plugins by stars, instant, **zero GitHub API calls**; - **插件 / 技能 tabs** next to the search box: the skills tab lists auto-collected `agent-skills` ∪ `claude-skills` ∪ `dsh-skill` repos (up to 300); - **Auto version check**: installed entries in the market are checked against npm `dist-tags.latest` in the background — cards turn into **「更新 → vX」** buttons; - **Skill install**: skill entries install by git-clone into `~/.dsh/skills//` (frontmatter `name` wins over repo name; SKILL.md found at repo root or first-level subdirectory). That version is carried into every download channel; if a channel ends up with a different version, the job reports a failure with both versions named, and the existing copy on disk is kept rather than replaced. The manifest and lock record a **version number** for such packages — a normal install does not produce a `link:`. Installs and updates are tracked per target: two different plugins can update at the same time, while the same plugin cannot be started twice. A finished install leaves two small records under `/plugin-console/`: - `pending-restart.json` — plugins that are installed but not yet loaded, so the panel can keep showing "installed · takes effect after restart" across a host restart. Entries are dropped once the plugin is actually loaded. - `install-jobs.json` — the last fifty settled jobs, with the requested version, the version that landed, and the error if any. A failure can therefore still be explained after the process that produced it is gone. Drift between the manifest and the lock is reconciled in the background with a cooldown, without blocking `/state`. Source-type dependencies (`link:`, `file:`, git) are excluded from that automation. A mismatch is reported as a failure only when it would actually lose the plugin; a lock or version drift is shown as a collapsible note instead. ### Dev links (`link`) `link:` is a **development** mechanism — ordinary download installs and updates do not produce it. The `link` entry in the feature-pack toolbar is the working surface for it: - pick a registered dev root from the dropdown, or type an absolute path; - **Pin** is a two-step action: it first returns a read-only plan, and executes only after you confirm. No code path skips that confirmation; - each row shows the target directory and its last-modified time, which is how you tell whether it is the directory you are editing right now; - per-row actions appear only when they apply — **fill dependencies**, **build shims** (no pnpm run), and **unpin**; - **Browse…** is rendered only when the desktop preload bridge is present. On a web instance it is not rendered, rather than shown as a button that cannot work. ### Disable provenance A row can be off for different reasons, and the panel distinguishes them: - **disabled by this console's patch** — removing the patch block enables it normally; - **disabled by the plugin or the framework default** — the console can only write an explicit `disabled: false` override, which is what the **forced on by patch** badge refers to; - **force-enable had no effect** — the override exists but the row still is not running, and no peer veto explains it. That override can be revoked from the row. ### Operational details - Market enrichment runs behind a single limiter: four concurrent requests, one in flight per URL, a ten-minute memory for failures and a five-minute success cache. A batch of unreachable mirrors therefore cannot saturate the connection or delay installs. - `Disk audit` lists what occupies `/plugin-console` and deletes only after an explicit confirmation. The framework rollback point counts as protected. - The gate panel shows the current pending adaptations up front and keeps its history collapsed. ## Known limitations - Host code changes require a **service restart**; client changes only need a page refresh. - On a **desktop-hosted** instance the console **refuses** to restart and says so: the official path is to fully quit and reopen the client.
